content:
luca: heads-up 1: customer (BetaMetrics) hit errors after switching to our batch embeddings endpoint. They see 'dimension mismatch' plus occasional 504s when batch_size > 32.

luca: customer's error payload: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  \"error\": \"EmbeddingDimensionError\",
  \"detail\": \"expected 1536, received 768\"
}
```

sophie: 768 -> sounds like an intermediate PCA or a 50% reduction quantization. Did they run a model that outputs 768? Which model are they calling?

anita: They called model \"redwood-open-1536\" per their request. They say they precompute embeddings via a legacy pipeline that used SVD reduction.

luca: Customer excerpt of request (redacted headers):
```
POST /v1/embeddings/batch
{
  \"model\":\"redwood-open-1536\",
  \"batch_size\":64,
  \"vectors\": [[...768 floats...],[...768 floats...], ...]
}
```

sophie: Two lanes here: 1) server should return a clearer actionable error when vectors don't match expected dims (eg. suggest desired length and link to docs). 2) our batching path should avoid turning mismatch into timeouts.

anita: infra-bot pulled logs for time window: many batches were partially processed, then worker timed out waiting for the rest of the batch --> cascade and 504s. Looks like the batcher waits up to 10s for batch to fill; with many invalid vectors the worker spends CPU validating and then rejecting, causing backlog.

infra-bot: Ticket created: SUP-9921. Linked to RD-5860 (batcher mixed-length detection) and RD-5861 (better embedding validation).

eng-embed: We tightened server-side validation in last stable release; older SDKs allowed mismatched dims and relied on our padding/trimming heuristics. That created silent data corruption. New behavior errs loudly. Possibly the customer upgraded the server SDK or our API changed.

luca: The customer claims no code change in their pipeline. They upgraded our client SDK from 0.9.x -> 1.3.x last week (per their changelog).

sophie: There we go. Client-side change + server validation results in immediate errors. For throughput: large batch sizes combined with validation rejections will make some workers retry; recommend they lower batch_size temporarily. Ask them to set batch_size=1 or <=8 to confirm.

anita: I'll prepare a short repro script they can run to show failing vs working requests. Also add a client-side check script to validate vector lengths before POSTing.

eng-embed: Proposed fixes: 
- Fast-fail on mixed/incorrect dims before scheduling into GPU batcher. Return HTTP 400 with message: \"Embedding length mismatch: expected 1536, got 768. If sending precomputed vectors, ensure they match the model embedding size; otherwise send raw text.\"
- Emit metric batch_mixed_length_count and alert when > 1% of embedding batches contain mixed lengths.
- Add compatibility header X-Allow-legacy-embeddings:true for enterprise customers that need to continue accepting legacy-length vectors (internal flag; requires acceptance of known risks).

billing-team: Note: if a customer switches from sending raw text (we compute embeddings) to uploading precomputed vectors, they may expect different billing treatment. Confirming whether BetaMetrics was charged differently during the incident.

luca: I'll ask BetaMetrics for: full request bodies/headers, SDK version, sample vectors (first 5 vectors as base64 or truncated), whether they intentionally reduced dimensions, and whether they used our `embeddings/batch` helper. Also offer: run a quick test with batch_size=1 and our client-side verifier.

sophie: Docs action: add an FAQ item "Why am I getting EmbeddingDimensionError?" with examples for: 
- sending raw text (recommended)
- sending precomputed vectors (must match model dim)
- sample curl and SDK checks
Include command-line verifier script and note about batching.

anita: I'll add a Support Runbook snippet: steps to triage dimension mismatch: 
1) Ask if vectors are precomputed or raw text.
2) If precomputed, ask for length of vectors and model name.
3) Ask them to retry with batch_size=1 and collect server trace id.
4) If still failing, request minimal reproducible example and escalate to eng-embed.

eng-embed: Also: investigate whether batching latency increases when many validation failures are observed. If yes, we need to change batcher scheduling to ignore invalid requests earlier.

infra-bot: Added runbook link to SUP-9921: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-9921 and docs stub PR draft created at https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4523

luca: I'll message the customer with repro steps + ask about billing expectations and offer a 30-min troubleshooting call.

sophie: One more ops note: for hosted customers in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, we should scan the last 24h for EmbeddingDimensionError and group by SDK version to see if this is a widespread regression.

anita: Running that scan now, will post results here.

(15 minutes later)

anita: Scan results: 12 customers in last 24h, 9 on SDK >=1.2.0. Error spike correlated with SDK 1.2+ rollout. I filed RD-5862 to add telemetry to SDK that warns when user-supplied vectors length != model dim before sending.

luca: OK. Plan of record:
- Support: send customer repro checklist + lower batch_size suggestion + client verifier script. Offer call. (luca)
- Docs: FAQ + runbook patch (sophie & anita)
- Eng: fast-fail + metrics + compatibility header (eng-embed)
- Billing: confirm any unexpected charges (billing-team)

luca: tagging follow-ups into SUP-9921. Will update when customer replies. :eyes:

(THREAD END)
